prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” broker that fits everyone — the right one depends on your ZIP code, age, budget, health needs, whether you want on‑exchange (ACA) coverage or a private/off‑exchange plan, and whether you want benefits for just yourself or for a small business/group plan. I can help find the best fit quickly, but first a few pointers and a way forward.

Questions that help me narrow it down
- Are you in Kansas City, Missouri (KC, MO) or Kansas (KC, KS)? (Marketplace rules and carrier availability can vary.)
- Single or family coverage? Ages and tobacco use?
- Do you want an ACA individual plan (with potential premium tax credits), short‑term coverage, or to set up a small group plan for your business?
- Any providers you must keep (doctors, prescriptions)?
- Do you prefer a local in‑person broker or are you fine using a reputable online broker?

How to choose a broker (quick checklist)
- Licensed in Missouri (verify at the Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance) and in Kansas if needed.
- Experience with ACA marketplace enrollments and with self‑employed clients.
- Independent (can quote many carriers) rather than captive to a single insurer.
- Transparent about commissions and any fees; willing to explain subsidies (premium tax credits) if you qualify.
- Good local reviews and references; membership in professional groups like NAHU (National Association of Health Underwriters) is a plus.
- Will provide written side‑by‑side comparisons, network/pharmacy checks, and ongoing year‑round service.

Places and resources to search immediately
- HealthCare.gov (federal marketplace) — certified navigators and agents can help with on‑exchange plans and subsidies.
- Local independent agencies — search Google/Yelp for “health insurance broker Kansas City MO” and look for high ratings and ACA experience.
- National online brokers that compare multiple carriers: HealthSherpa, eHealth, GoHealth — useful for quick quotes (but confirm whether they show on‑exchange subsidy-eligible plans).
- Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance — to verify agent licensing and complaints.
- Local NAHU chapter (Kansas City) — they can refer experienced brokers.

If you want, I can:
- Pull a short list of 3–5 well‑rated local Kansas City brokers/agents (with phone/email/links) if you give your ZIP code, or
- Compare 3 plan quotes (on‑exchange and off‑exchange) if you give age(s), ZIP, and expected 2026 income range.

Which would you prefer?
